notes: [P1] robustness: in src/main.js, `const storage = globalThis.localStorage` runs at module top level, outside any try. Some browsers throw a SecurityError just from reading the `localStorage` property when site data is blocked (for example Chrome with cookies disabled, or some sandboxed iframes). In that setting the whole game would fail to boot, which did not happen before this change. best.js says a storage that throws reads as no best, but it can only catch errors from getItem and setItem, not from this property read. Wrap the read in a try (for example `let storage; try { storage = globalThis.localStorage; } catch { storage = undefined; }`). No test covers this, and normal setups never hit it, so this is a follow-up, not a miss against the brief.

[P2] scope: best.js adds `bestAfterStep`, a function the brief did not ask for. It puts main.js's 'a run ends on the playing→won/lost step' rule in best.js so it can be tested, which is reasonable. But best.js now encodes knowledge of the game's status values, which is more than the storage-only module the issue describes (`readBest`/`writeBest`).

[P2] test-structure: the end-to-end loss test (test/best.test.js:133-148) runs the real `step` for up to 2000 frames and assumes a game with 1 life is lost within 100 simulated seconds. If wave timing or the game's balance changes, the test could fail even though best.js is still correct.
